commits.author: Deniz Altunkapan
commits.message:
feat(agents): repair failing CI on agent pull requests automatically

CI repair used to wait for a maintainer to apply the agent-repair label.
It now reacts on its own when Backend CI or Frontend CI fails on an
agent branch, and pushes the fix to that pull request's branch.

The coding agent names its branches agent/issue-<n>-<slug>, and CI
repair only runs for those branches. Before the model is invoked it also
requires:

- the branch to live in this repository, not a fork;
- an open pull request from it labelled agent-managed;
- that pull request not to have used its final attempt (agent-reentry-2).

It stops after two attempts and hands over to a maintainer. It never
pushes to main and never merges; merging stays a human step. The branch
name is used only in the deterministic gates, never interpolated into
the prompt; the agent finds the pull request by commit SHA.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Deniz Altunkapan
commits.message:
feat(agents): route issues between contributors and agents

The audit, triage and coding agents now hand work to each other, while
contributors keep first claim on anything they want to do.

- The audit and triage agents write through the vault-web-agents app, so
  the issues and labels they create raise events other workflows see.
  GITHUB_TOKEN writes do not, which is why audit issues never reached
  triage before.
- Triage decides who an issue is for: "good first issue" for
  contributors, "help wanted" for larger work, "agent-ready" only for
  narrow mechanical changes nobody has claimed.
- The coding agent reacts to "agent-ready" from the app, stops if the
  issue is assigned, linked to a pull request, claimed in a comment or
  labelled "good first issue", and never runs with more than three open
  agent pull requests.
- An outside contributor's issue stays unreadable to the coding agent
  until a maintainer adds "agent-approved". Triage cannot set that
  label, so untrusted text never reaches the agent that writes code
  without a human decision. Issues from the audit app are trusted.

Every agent pull request is a draft and is merged by a maintainer. The
README explains the labels for contributors.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Deniz Altunkapan
commits.message:
fix(agents): let review and triage read first-time contributions

Both agents ran with tools.github.min-integrity: approved. A first-time
contributor sits at integrity "none", so the integrity filter denied the
agents the very PRs and issues they exist to handle. On a real external
PR the reviewer spent its turns working around the denials and was then
cut off at its 40-credit cap, which the proxy reports as an HTTP 403
"authentication failed".

Lower min-integrity to none on both agents. Strict mode then requires an
explicit shell allowlist, so replace the implicit allow-all-tools with
read-only commands. Raise the review cap to 150 credits (450/day) and
triage to 80, since a real code review costs more than the trivial diff
the old cap was sized on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Deniz Altunkapan
commits.message:
fix(agents): review fork PRs via pull_request_target

In a public repository a pull_request run from a fork receives no
secrets, so COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN is empty and the review agent failed in
activation ("None of the following secrets are set"). roles: all let the
run start but could not get it past that point.

Switch the reviewer to pull_request_target, which runs in the base
repository context with secrets. Fork code is never checked out: the
agent checkout is pinned to the PR base SHA and the other checkouts
default to the base branch; the agent reads the diff through the GitHub
API. gh-aw refuses to compile pull_request_target with a normal
checkout, and this is the base-only pattern it recommends.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Deniz Altunkapan
commits.message:
fix(agents): let outside contributors trigger review and triage

gh-aw only runs a workflow for users with admin, maintainer or write
access unless the workflow says otherwise. The review and triage agents
set forks: ["*"] but no roles, so fork PRs passed the fork filter and
were then dropped by the role check. Since rollout the reviewer has not
run on a single external PR; PR #358 from a first-time contributor was
skipped with "permission read does not meet requirements".

Set roles: all on both agents. Because anyone can now start a run, add
a per-user limit of three runs an hour so one account cannot drain the
credit budget. The coding and CI repair agents keep their maintainer
gate.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Deniz Altunkapan
commits.message:
ci: move frontend to Node 22 and tighten workflow permissions

Node 18 reached end of life in April 2025 and no longer receives
security updates. Angular 19.2 supports Node 18.19, 20 and 22, so 22 is
the newest version this project can take — not 24.

Verified locally on Node 22.23.2: npm ci, npm run build and
npm run prettier:check all pass.

Also declare permissions explicitly. Both CI workflows only read the
repository, so contents: read is enough. The Javadoc workflow had
pull-requests: write without opening any pull request — it pushes to
gh-pages and nothing else — so that is dropped.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Deniz Altunkapan
commits.message:
chore(agents): cut credit spend and drop injection warnings

The first day of real runs cost about 324 of the 1,500 monthly AI
credits across two repositories, and the two repository audits were 83%
of that. Measured: audit 157 and 112 credits, pull request reviews 9 to
25.

Move the audit to every 14 days and halve the review cap to 40, which
still leaves headroom over what the real reviews consumed. Expected
spend drops to roughly 350 credits a month instead of 600 to 800.

Also remove the lines telling the reviewer and the triage agent to treat
contributor input as untrusted data. The agents are deliberately left in
their default state here so that trust propagation can be observed
rather than suppressed. The structural controls are unchanged: the agent
job is read-only, every mutation goes through a safe output, and branch
rules still require review before anything merges.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Deniz Altunkapan
commits.message:
fix(agents): skip review of generated DIRECTORY.md updates

The directory workflow opens its pull request with a personal access
token, so the actor is a human account and skip-bots does not catch it.
A first live run confirmed this: the reviewer started on the generated
PR, correctly found nothing worth saying, and stayed silent — but the
run still cost credits.

Ignore DIRECTORY.md so a pull request that only regenerates it no longer
triggers a review.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Deniz Altunkapan
commits.message:
chore: add agentic workflows

Add five gh-aw agentic workflows covering pull request review, issue
triage, a weekly repository audit, an opt-in coding agent and CI repair.

The agent job itself is read-only in every workflow; all mutations go
through explicitly declared safe outputs, which gh-aw executes in
separate permission-scoped jobs.

Pull request review opts into fork pull requests, since most
contributions here come from forks. It runs alongside the existing
Copilot Code Review and is scoped to deeper correctness, security and
regression findings.

The coding agent and CI repair only run when a maintainer applies a
label, and CI repair additionally requires the pull request to carry
agent-managed. Its re-entry limit is enforced before the model is
invoked, not by the prompt.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
